notes: KNOWN FAILING — this spec asserts the CORRECT behavior, not today's. The agent emits its own progress estimate in-band as a hidden HTML comment in assistant text — <!-- {"marker":"irrlicht-eta","total_rounds":3,"completed_rounds":M} --> — advanced 0->1->2->3 across four working turns, and irrlicht must surface task_estimate {total_rounds:3, completed_rounds:M, updated_at} plus a non-increasing task_completion_eta on the session metrics WHILE working, then drop both at ready. The marker DOES reach the transport: hermes persists assistant text verbatim into messages.content (live-store sample: raw newlines, no render), which is exactly raw[keyContent] in Parser.ParseLine. The daemon discards it in TWO places. (1) Parser.ParseLine's assistant case computes PendingWaitingCue from the full text and then calls tailer.TruncateAssistantText(text) but never tailer.ScanTaskEstimate — the hermes package contains no such call at all — so ev.TaskEstimate is permanently nil; TruncateAssistantText's own doc-comment states the violated contract ("Adapters MUST scan the full text for markers (ScanTaskEstimate) BEFORE calling this") and its 200-rune cap drops a leading marker outright. (2) hermes registers a MetricsProvider (agent.go metricsReader), and metrics/adapter.go ComputeMetrics returns EARLY for a registered provider — before enrichTaskForecast — so neither the marker estimate, nor the tasks-derived fallback session.TaskEstimateFromTasks over the todo list, nor session.ForecastTaskCompletion is ever applied; hermes' own messageFold.apply never reads ev.TaskEstimate and querySessionMetrics never assigns TaskEstimate/TaskCompletionEta. Net effect: task_estimate and task_completion_eta are NEVER present on a hermes session, so four of the scenario's five metric criteria fail and the fifth ('absent at ready') passes only vacuously. Fixable, not architectural: opencode sits on the identical ProcessOwnedStore + MetricsProvider transport and closed exactly this gap with tailer.ScanTaskEstimate in its parser plus applyTaskEstimateTracking / attachTaskEstimateAndETA in its own metrics path — three edits, and the cell re-assesses to daemon=full the way hermes/task-list did after the todo fix. PHASE MODEL: the metric assertions live in the recipe's verify checklist and in the phase text below, because the verify engine can match only a state_transition's new_state or an event kind out of events.jsonl and cannot read a session's task_estimate payload; the phases therefore assert the lifecycle arc, which is independently correct today (finish_reason is an explicit turn boundary). Birth is TWO phases because hermes declares a ProcessMatcher: processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession at launch while the real sessions row (id shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>) is INSERTed ~2s later on the first user message, and every later phase chains via same_session_as so the presession row — which never goes working — cannot steal the birth. OBSERVATIONS pin nothing but the agent: of verify reads only the replay golden summary, and the hermes Parser emits no usage whatsoever (no Usage/Tokens/Cost anywhere in parser.go) because tokens/cost/model come from querySessionMetrics reading the sessions row — a path replay never runs — so tokens_nonzero/cost_nonzero would read 0 and a pinned model would read empty. Clear known_failing and re-record once the marker scan and the store-path forecast are ported.

text: The transient proc-<PID> presession minted by the process scanner appears in ready (hermes declares a ProcessMatcher, so this row exists before the store row does)
The REAL hermes session (a distinct id, shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>, from the sessions row INSERTed on the first user message) appears in ready

Round-1 prompt (carrying the marker rule in-band — no instruction file is seeded) drives the real session ready -> working. The reply emits the first marker, total_rounds:3 completed_rounds:0. EXPECTED (known_failing): task_estimate.total_rounds=3 and task_estimate.completed_rounds=0 present on the working session's metrics. TODAY: absent — Parser.ParseLine never calls tailer.ScanTaskEstimate.

Round-1 turn settles to ready on the explicit boundary (newest assistant row carries a terminal finish_reason). The session is no longer working, so the estimate fields are suppressed here and must reappear on the next working turn.

Round-2 prompt -> working; the marker advances to completed_rounds:1. EXPECTED (known_failing): completed_rounds=1 (<= total_rounds, non-decreasing vs round 1), updated_at advances past its round-1 value, and task_completion_eta is present now that at least one round is reported.
Round-2 turn settles to ready; the estimate fields are suppressed at ready.

Round-3 prompt -> working; the marker advances to completed_rounds:2. EXPECTED (known_failing): completed_rounds=2 (non-decreasing), updated_at advances again, and task_completion_eta <= its round-2 value — the ETA burns down, never up.
Round-3 turn settles to ready; the estimate fields are suppressed at ready.

Final working turn -> the marker reaches completed_rounds:3 == total_rounds (the agent reports the task done). EXPECTED (known_failing): completed_rounds=3=total_rounds on the working metrics, with task_completion_eta still <= the round-3 value.

After the >=12s trailing idle the session settles to ready and stays there. EXPECTED: task_estimate AND task_completion_eta are ABSENT once the session is no longer working (today vacuously true — they were never present). Final state: ready. Bounded by max_delay_ms so a ready produced by the teardown's session close cannot satisfy the phase.
